notes: The data originate from a randomised evaluation of a school-based nutrition intervention in Jehanabad district, Bihar, India, with high anaemia prevalence among school-aged children. The intervention introduced Double Fortified Salt (DFS) into the Mid-Day Meal (MDM) programme across 107 public primary and middle schools. In 2015, 54 schools were randomly assigned to early treatment and began receiving DFS; the remaining 53 served as controls until December 2017, when they transitioned to treatment, creating early and late treatment groups. Survey data were collected at three points in time: baseline (2014), midline (2016), and endline (2019). This phase-in design generates approximately four years of DFS exposure for early treatment schools and one and a half years for late treatment schools. The longitudinal structure supports tracking of individual children over time, enabling double-differences estimation with child fixed effects to identify causal impacts. Child-level data. The dataset contains rich information on children's health, cognitive, and educational outcomes. Health outcomes include haemoglobin levels, anaemia status (overall, mild, and moderate-to-severe), and anthropometric measures. Cognitive outcomes were assessed using standardised tests; educational outcomes cover attendance, grade progression, and related indicators. Demographic and socio-economic variables — including age, gender, household characteristics, and parental background — are also available. School-level data. Three instruments were administered at each survey wave. Headmaster interviews captured school characteristics, enrolment, MDM management practices, infrastructure, and MDM implementation. Cook-cum-helper interviews gathered information on working conditions, food preparation practices, and ingredient measurement procedures. School observations recorded infrastructure, hygiene conditions, kitchen facilities, and the meal preparation and distribution process.
